STEVENSON

Aerospace Engineering — University of Surrey

Second-year aerospace engineer at the University of Surrey, working trackside with Formula 1 teams and building motorsport and aerospace projects in his own time. Applying for placement year positions in motorsport / aerospace engineering.

Between my Aerospace Engineering degree, hands-on CFD work in ANSYS Fluent on my Formula Student side flicks, and designing my own open tabletop wind tunnel to deepen my understanding of testing methodology, I can confidently say I have a strong foundational understanding of race car aerodynamic principles and concepts. This foundation isn't purely academic — it's been shaped by wider reading such as Carroll Smith's Tune to Win, close collaboration with my Formula Student teammates, and a habit of questioning engineers wherever I get the chance. Trackside at Shelsley Walsh, I had extensive discussions with Sean Gould about the design of his championship-winning Gould GR59, and with Willem Toet about his Empire Wraith — both dominant cars in the British Hill Climb Championship — having gone along with Andy Greenen, who now drives one. Separately, I spoke with senior F1 aerodynamicist Stefano Nitti about what it actually takes to break into the discipline. Together, these experiences have shaped how I approach my own projects.

Projects

01 Fixed Wing FPV Drone with Flight Controller — "Icarus"
FLIGHT TEST +

Self-designed fixed-wing FPV aircraft with hand-calculated aerodynamics and simulated in XFLR5, now on its second iteration. V1 was a 3D-printed ABS delta wing — too heavy and needed a runway to get airborne. It crashed repeatedly on takeoff attempts, eventually splitting in two, which sent the design back to the drawing board. V2 moved to a conventional straight-wing layout with a longer span, printed in foaming LW-PLA with PETG used for parts that needed to stay ductile, with carbon-fibre spars added through the wings for rigidity. Both versions are fully modelled in Fusion 360, and both were built. The V-tail was sized using tail volume coefficient theory — the standard empennage-sizing method in stability & control texts (Raymer, Roskam) — applying Selberg & Cronin's equivalent-tail decomposition to split the V-tail into an equivalent horizontal and vertical tail, with the 30° dihedral set by the ratio of their required areas.

WING610mm span, NACA 4412
TAILV-tail ruddervator, NACA 0008, 30° dihedral
WEIGHT~700g
PERFORMANCEStall ~7 m/s, hand-launched (XFLR5)
CONSTRUCTIONFoaming LW-PLA + PETG (ductile parts), carbon-fibre wing spars
STORAGEWings removable via a bespoke PETG screw-and-nut system
FEATUREBlown-wing effect; drooped wingtips double as landing gear
CADV1 and V2 both fully modelled in Fusion 360, and both built
V1 → V2Grey ABS delta wing (V1) too heavy, crashed repeatedly on takeoff and split in two — rebuilt as black LW-PLA straight wing (V2), see photos. Takeoff itself was the main factor behind the crashes, so V2 moved from a runway takeoff to a hand launch

02 Formula Student Side Flicks
SURTES FS +

Aerodynamic side flick design for the SURTES Formula Student car, designed largely independently in first year with guidance from more experienced teammates. Various concept designs were explored before committing to CAD; once a basic shape was settled, different aerofoils were tested. The aerofoils selected were kept the same as the front wing's secondary and tertiary elements to save on cost. AOA, aerofoil, and chord were then adjusted in CAD and simulated in ANSYS Fluent until they behaved as intended across an average velocity — producing downforce while also reducing drag by redirecting air around the rear wheels, cutting tyre wake and rotational drag.

06 Single Seater Hill-Climb Car — Concept Design
CONCEPT ONLY +

A concept-stage design exercise, not a committed build — worked through as a self-directed engineering study for UK club hillclimb and sprint competition (Prescott, Shelsley Walsh, Harewood), targeting Motorsport UK Blue Book compliance around a Kawasaki Z1000 powertrain.

CHASSISSteel spaceframe, ERW220 tube, ~2450mm wheelbase
SUSPENSIONFront pullrod / rear pushrod monoshock, MR 1.15:1 / 0.75:1
DAMPERSAVO 10" coilovers, 63.5mm stroke
ROLL CONTROLBelleville washer springs, no roll damping — deliberate trade-off
UPRIGHTSBespoke CNC 7075-T6 aluminium, all four corners
DRIVETRAINChain final drive, Fiesta-based diff → Quaife ATB, custom driveshafts
TOOLSFusion 360, MATLAB (suspension geometry & camber-gain scripts)
MODELLINGAll parts fully modelled — spaceframe (with quotes obtained from laser cutting companies), suspension, uprights, wheels, wishbones
